app.title: Eden Settings
status.title: Status
status.hint.running: Settings are locked while Eden is running, because Eden rewrites its own settings when it closes. Close the game first (Steam+B).
status.hint.idle: Changes apply the next time you start a game.
status.notFound.title: Eden not found
status.notFound.body: No Eden settings file was found. Install Eden (Flatpak: dev.eden_emu.eden) and start it once, then reopen this panel.
section.global.hint: Defaults for every game. A game can override them in the Per game section.
game.pick.desc: Pick a game, then change only what that game needs. “Global” means: follow the global setting.
game.customNone: This game follows the global settings
game.none: No games found. Put your .nsp or .xci files in ~/Emulation/switch/games, or add a folder in Eden's game list.
game.reset.desc: Removes all custom settings of this game. Your global settings stay as they are.
shortcut.add.desc: Creates a Game Mode tile that starts Eden fullscreen with this game, with artwork. Eden's own settings are not touched.
shortcut.noIcon: No icon found for this game, so the artwork will only show the title. To get its icon, put “{id}-icon.jpg” in an “artwork” folder next to your games folder.
shortcut.remove.desc: The tile “{name}” is in your Steam library. Removing it deletes the tile only, not the game.
shortcut.noPath: The game file was not found, so no Steam tile can be made for it.

setting.resolution_setup.label: Resolution
setting.resolution_setup.desc: Internal render resolution. 1x is the Switch's own resolution (1080p docked, 720p handheld). Higher is sharper but needs much more GPU power and video memory.
setting.scaling_filter.label: Upscaling filter
setting.scaling_filter.desc: How the picture is scaled to your screen. AMD FSR gives the sharpest result when the game renders below your screen size. Bilinear is soft and cheap; Nearest keeps hard pixels.
setting.fsr_sharpening_slider.label: FSR sharpness
setting.fsr_sharpening_slider.desc: Only used with the AMD FSR filter. Higher adds more contrast to edges; very high values look harsh.
setting.anti_aliasing.label: Anti-aliasing
setting.anti_aliasing.desc: Smooths jagged edges. SMAA looks best, FXAA is cheaper and helps at low resolutions. Off is fastest.
setting.max_anisotropy.label: Anisotropic filtering
setting.max_anisotropy.desc: Keeps textures sharp at steep angles, such as roads and floors. 16x costs very little on most GPUs.
setting.aspect_ratio.label: Aspect ratio
setting.aspect_ratio.desc: Stretches the picture to another shape. Most games are made for 16:9, so other ratios look stretched unless the game is modded. “Stretch” fills the whole window.
setting.use_docked_mode.label: Console mode
setting.use_docked_mode.desc: Docked is TV mode: 1080p and all controllers. Handheld renders at 720p and is lighter on your GPU. Some games change their detail level with this.
setting.vram_usage_mode.label: Video memory use
setting.vram_usage_mode.desc: Conservative saves video memory. Aggressive uses as much as it can for fewer stutters, but may starve other apps such as recorders.
setting.use_vsync.label: VSync mode
setting.use_vsync.desc: FIFO: no tearing, locked to your screen's refresh rate (safe default). FIFO Relaxed: tears when the game runs slow. Mailbox: low latency, no tearing, may drop frames. Immediate: no sync, lowest latency, tearing.
setting.use_speed_limit.label: Speed limit
setting.use_speed_limit.desc: On keeps the game at normal speed. Off unlocks the frame rate: the game runs as fast as your PC allows, which can make some games run too fast.
setting.speed_limit.label: Speed limit (%)
setting.speed_limit.desc: Only used when the speed limit is on. 100% is normal speed. 200% turns a 30 fps game into 60 fps (and 60 into 120), if the game allows it.
setting.force_max_clock.label: Force maximum GPU clock
setting.force_max_clock.desc: Stops the GPU from lowering its clock while it waits. Can fix stutter and uneven frame pacing; uses a little more power.
setting.use_asynchronous_shaders.label: Asynchronous shaders
setting.use_asynchronous_shaders.desc: Compiles shaders in the background to reduce stutter. Objects may briefly be missing or look wrong until their shader is ready.
setting.rescale_hack.label: Rescale hack
setting.rescale_hack.desc: Workaround for games that show broken or missing graphics above 1x resolution. Only turn it on if a game looks wrong when upscaled.
setting.nvdec_emulation.label: Video decoding (cutscenes)
setting.nvdec_emulation.desc: How in-game videos are decoded. GPU is fastest and right for most games. Try CPU if videos glitch. Off skips decoding, so videos stay black.
